{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Sweden|Swedish Cuisine]]

'''Kroppkakor''' is a traditional Swedish dish of potato [[Cookbook:dumpling|dumplings]] with a pork or bacon filling. They are cooked and served with butter and [[Cookbook:Lingonberry|lingonberry]] [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]]. There are some regional variations to the recipe.

== Ingredients == 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] cooked [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], mashed
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]]
* 1 ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:flour|all-purpose flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] smoked [[Cookbook:ham|ham]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 100 g [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], diced
* White [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:allspice|Allspice]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
# Mound the mashed potatoes on a work surface and make an indentation in the middle.
# Put yolks, flour, and salt in the indentation, and quickly work into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. Too much kneading will make the dough tough. Let it rest for a few minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the onions until translucent. Add the bacon and ham, and cook until it gets colored. Season with pepper.
# Shape the dough into a thick log. Cut the log into thick slices, and make an indentation in each slice.
# Place some of the onion and meat filling in the indentation, and top with another dough slice. Press the edges together to seal, and roll into a ball.
# Lower the balls into [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] salted water, and boil them for about 10–12 minutes or until they float to the surface. Don’t boil too many at a time, as they will then have some difficulty floating to the surface.
# Remove them with a perforated spoon, and transfer them to a hot serving plate. 
# Serve hot with melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] and red whortleberry ([[Cookbook:Lingonberry|lingonberry]]) or [[Cookbook:Cranberry|cranberry]] jam.
